data.single_linear: PhD Researcher advancing Trustworthy AI through Explainable Machine Learning, Adversarial Robustness, and Open-World Learning.
data.about_me: I am a PhD student in Data Science and Engineering at the University of South Dakota, working on Trustworthy AI with a focus on Explainable AI, Adversarial Robustness, and Open-World Learning. My research explores how intelligent systems can remain interpretable, robust, and reliable, particularly when encountering previously unseen information. My work has been published in venues including NeurIPS, AAAI, and IEEE JBHI. Before entering academia, I spent nearly five years as a Software Engineer developing production applications across healthcare, financial services, and international tax research. This combination of research and industry experience shapes my approach to building AI systems that are not only theoretically sound but also practical and reliable.
data.research_vision:
My research is driven by a fundamental question: How do we build AI systems that are truly worthy of trust?
As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into critical domains, accuracy alone is no longer sufficient. Intelligent systems must be interpretable, robust against adversarial threats, and capable of recognizing the limits of their own knowledge.
My work lies at the intersection of Explainable AI, Adversarial Robustness, and Open-World Learning. I am particularly interested in developing models that can explain their decisions through human-understandable concepts, remain resilient under challenging conditions, and discover previously unseen categories without sacrificing interpretability. Through concept-based representations and principled learning methods, I aim to bridge the gap between predictive performance and meaningful understanding.
I believe trustworthy AI should not be an additional feature introduced after a model has been developed. Explainability, robustness, and reliability should be fundamental properties of intelligent systems.
Before pursuing research, I spent nearly five years as a Software Engineer building production applications across healthcare and international business platforms. That experience continues to shape my research philosophy: advancing theoretical understanding while developing practical methods that can translate into reliable, real-world AI systems.
